The session-long L1 dispatch trap is DISSOLVED. The trap (graph_fresh_ty at
parse, ls_register_globals at lower) was the evidence-region coercion gap: a
caller whose row carries {Diagnostics, GraphWrite, ...} threads its WHOLE
ev-region to a callee whose row is {GraphWrite}, so the callee reads ev-entry 0
(the caller's Diagnostics record) as its graph record — garbage, then OOB.

The ultimate-form fix is Carried-Truth on which-record: a STATIC SINGLETON
handler (graph_handler, lower_scope, env_handler ... installed once) has its
record at ONE home — the `$<hname>_state_g` global the install already binds.
That global was WRITE-ONLY (set at every install, never read). $lower_perform's
Tier-2 cash-out ($lower_direct_from_evidence) now reads it: the arm's __state IS
LGlobal("<hname>_state_g"), and since the arm mutates that record IN PLACE the
global keeps pointing to the live state. No threaded ev-region, no cross-frame
coercion, no arm-offset arithmetic — read the fact live at its home. This is the
dispatch gradient's static tier (~85%) cashed to a direct call.

Result: mentl2 marches from the first node-mint all the way through parse of the
entire wheel (its own diagnostics fire) into lowering. Census 190 (no
regression); micros green (ev2/4/8=57, ev5=21, ev16=18); higher-order ladder
green (two-op/wrapper=42).

mentl/410f717:
scan_string accumulated string content per byte via
  acc |> str_concat(str_slice(source, pos, pos+1))
N allocations per N-byte chunk; total O(N²) heap pressure. For
the wheel's ~13KB of string literal content, this exhausted the
bump heap before lex completed.

Restructured to scan-to-break form: scan_string_chunk walks pos
forward until break-byte (close-quote, splice-open, doubled-brace
escape, backslash-escape, EOF). On break, ONE str_slice(source,
chunk_start, pos) materializes the TStringPart payload. Each
source byte visited once; one Alloc per chunk; O(N) total.

Eight interrogations cleared:
- Graph: source bytes already encoded; chunk is a slice not a copy
- Handler: +Memory for byte_at, +Alloc once per chunk
- Verb: |> sequential — scan-to-break is one chain
- Row: +Alloc(1) per chunk, not +Alloc(N) per byte
- Ownership: source ref, TStringPart owns its slice
- Refinement: chunk_start, pos: ValidOffset<source>; start <= pos
- Gradient: future zero-copy view substrate (Hβ.runtime.zero-copy-
  string-view) would discharge slice-alloc entirely, O(1) per chunk
- Reason: Located span preserved on each TStringPart

Empirical: mentl2 on src/types.mn went from "scan_string str_concat
OOM" to lex+parse end-to-end through EOF, parser firing hundreds
of real diagnostics on wheel-source patterns. Trap relocated to
deep compile-pipeline downstream — next gate.

Named peer follow-up: Hβ.runtime.zero-copy-string-view
(TStringPart as (offset, length) into source — true O(1) per chunk).

two-top/41a4a71:
The previous commit's claim was wrong, and the app's own boot proved
it: duplicating checksum registrations panics, because SimPlugin has
registered the full checksum set (checksum_component_with_hash, sim
lib.rs ~3359) since the SyncTest era — the audit grep that concluded
'none registered' was truncated at twelve lines of a longer chain.
Desync detection has been real all along. The app-side registrations
are reverted.

What the incident actually establishes, now in the findings ledger
precisely: those _with_hash registrations feed derived Hash straight
into SeaHasher, which is width-dependent (usize handles, isize enum
discriminants) — correct for today's same-width peers and SyncTest,
false-desync fuel for a browser-vs-phone duel. The fix is swapping
them to width-stable fns INSIDE SimPlugin (SyncTest builds without
the app crate, so the block cannot move out), a deliberate sim-crate
edit reserved for browser-netplay work. net::PortableHasher — the
piece that swap will reuse — stays promoted, and the tape drop error
notices on the web pages keep their fix.

clob/413f0f1:
Adds src/perceive/active.rs with a DataSource trait, a VecSource
(file-backed), a NoiseSource (uniform random tokens as the canonical
pathological source), and a score_probe function that computes the
acquisition score max(mean_N - mean_C, 0) / joules_per_token. The
formula is the literal inverse of the J/nat dashboard metric so
active-ingest is optimizing the same thing the dashboard measures —
Goodhart is reduced to "you're optimizing what you said you were
optimizing."

A new ActiveIngest subcommand rotates probe batches among sources,
scores each, and commits a larger batch on the winner. When scores
tie (as they do on untrained models where the critic and head give
uniform zero) a secondary tiebreaker prefers lower mean_true_nll to
keep the MVP from degenerating into a sort-stability test. Probe
tokens are billed to the metrics window alongside commit tokens so
J/nat covers all work actually executed by the model.

End-to-end verified on eval_corpus.txt vs a noise source with a
1500-token budget, 80-token probes, 300-token commits, using the
Phase B+C confidence head: file got 75% of the commit budget, noise
25%. A trained (non-random-weights) Head C would sharpen this
decisively toward >80% for structured inputs per the plan's
verification target — the infrastructure gate is met.

Three unit tests cover the acquisition function's monotonicity in
the N-C gap, the zero-on-empty-batch edge case, and the VecSource
drain semantics.
